sealed: Written and committed before src/gemini.mjs, its tests, the command line's --harness gemini or tools/measure-6.mjs existed. Disclosed: the spec's recorder step says to start with Claude Code and one other harness, and the page listed one harness as a limit; Gemini CLI is the other harness on this machine. Its saved-session format was read from this machine's three saved sessions before sealing: the shape of each line, message ids and types, tool-call names and statuses, and the model names; no message text, tool arguments or results were read out. H1 and H2 are measured on those same three sessions, a small sample (4 tool calls), and say so. tools/measure-6.mjs refuses to run if this file differs from the commit that sealed it. A claim that fails is kept.
what: Organ 6, a second harness: a finished Gemini CLI session, read from its saved chat file (one JSON object a line), turned into a process record so it can be judged like any other. The format as found: a header line (sessionId, projectHash, startTime, lastUpdated, kind); lines of the form {$set: {...}} that update the session, where a $set of messages replaces the list of messages; and message lines (id, timestamp, type user or gemini, content, and on a reply its model and any toolCalls, each with an id, a name, a status and a timestamp). A message written again with the same id replaces the earlier version in its place: that is how a reply gains its tool calls. Each Gemini reply becomes a model call (its model, its time) and each of its tool calls a tool use (its name, its time), in order. Like organ 2's import of a Claude Code transcript, a past session sealed no intent, and the record says so ("none sealed"), so P1 fails. Pure apart from the intent's hash, and total.
data: Real sessions: every Gemini CLI session saved on this machine under ~/.gemini/tmp/*/chats (3 at sealing). They are private: read on this machine, and the receipt holds only counts. CI cannot hold them, so H1 and H2 are local; H3 to H5 run in CI on seeded synthetic sessions in the same format.
seenBefore: The structure of the three sessions, as described under sealed. Nothing has been imported or judged.
scope: An import after the job, not a live recorder: Gemini CLI is not hooked here, so no intent can be sealed before its work, and every imported record fails P1 by design. Tool calls are recorded by name and time; their arguments and results are not kept, and no file is kept as an artifact, so P7 fails too. Gemini CLI's saved format is not documented as stable: this reads it as found, and a later version may need the importer changed.

claims.claim: Import is faithful on real sessions: for every Gemini CLI session saved on this machine, the imported record holds exactly the session's tool calls (each distinct tool-call id, in the order first written, by name) and one model call per distinct Gemini reply, as counted by a separate reading of the raw lines; and every imported record fits the strict schema (P0 passes).
A past session is never dressed up: every imported real session, having no sealed intent, fails P1, and its intent's goal says none was sealed.

The format as found: for 500 seeded synthetic sessions in that format (a header, $set lines, user and Gemini messages, replies written again with their tool calls, and a $set of messages that replaces the list), the import gives exactly the events the generator meant, in order: one model call per reply with its model and time, then one tool use per tool call with its name and time.

Total: 2,000 garbage inputs (lines that are not JSON or not an object, lines of the wrong shape or with fields of the wrong type, and synthetic sessions cut at a random point) never make the importer throw; each line that is not a JSON object is counted as unreadable; and the strict rubric judges every record it gives without throwing.

The command line: acg import --harness gemini <session.jsonl> --out F writes a record whose harness is gemini-cli and whose tool uses are the session's, by name and in order; acg judge F judges it, and P1 fails.
